messages:
sre-oncall: FYI eu-central had a control-plane blip after a rapid GPU provisioning wave at 08:46 UTC. apiserver watch reconnects and controller-manager leader churn.
jena: noticed elevated accept queue and some 502/503s on the apiserver. any NAT/conntrack signs?
infra-bot: conntrack_util eu-central = 92% (threshold 90%) :warning: ; nat_ephemeral_used = 15670 / 16384
samir: provisioning job 'train-sprint' created ~300 pods, cluster tried to attach ~60 GPUs in 3m. kubelets opened many short-lived control connections.
paul: sample proxy error: `E0507 08:46:12.123 proxy.go:88] dial tcp 10.5.4.3:6443: connection reset by peer`
anna: etcd metrics show leader on ec1-b-04 with commit latency spiking to 180ms during the event. follower RTTs jumped too.
sre-oncall: hypothesis: provisioning storm -> conntrack + ephemeral port squeeze -> apiserver accept pressure -> watchers reconnect -> controller-manager leader backoff -> etcd election jitter.
jena: short mitigations: 1) hold GPU autoscaler for eu-central for 20m, 2) bump conntrack and ephemeral range on NATs, 3) move etcd leader off noisy host.
samir: applying autoscaler hold now.
paul: rolling sysctl: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=350000` and `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"` on NAT instances.
infra-bot: sysctl rollout triggered -> 12/12 gateways updated :white_check_mark:
anna: cordoning ec1-b-04 for control-plane, requesting leader transfer. leader moved to ec1-a-01 and commit latency fell to ~30ms.
sre-oncall: apiserver 5xxs trending down, controller-manager resumed steady leader lease.
jena: follow-ups: add autoscaler safety window for GPU pools, add ephemeral port headroom alert (75% -> p1), and add preflight that detects mass pod startups.
samir: will also add pod startup jitter to training job templates.
paul: note for infra: prefer placing etcd leaders on nodes with low local IO and away from ephemeral GPU churn.
sre-oncall: logging incident, scheduling 45m postmortem. tagging ENG-PLATFORM and COST. closing when stable. :thumbsup:
